exposure: single-layer uterine suturing technique during cesarean section
double-layer uterine suturing technique during cesarean section
outcome: appearance and localization of uterine scars
cohort: Women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies who underwent elective or acute cesarean section were randomly allocated to a uterine closure technique group.
finding: The double-layer suturing technique for uterine closure during cesarean section is associated with better suture healing and greater residual myometrial thickness compared to the single-layer technique.
mod_finding: The double-layer uterine closure technique during cesarean section resulted in a lower proportion of defects, wider defects, and thinner residual myometrial thickness compared to the single-layer technique.
